title: The projective-line calculation before purity
statement:
Let $N\geq1$, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $NA=0$, and let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme on which $N$ is invertible. Here Noetherian means having a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. Put $P=\mathbf P^1_S$ with projection $q:P\to S$. Work on small ordinary etale sites and their unbounded derived categories of constant-ring $A$-module sheaves. Define $A_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}A_T$ and $A_T(-1)=\mathcal Hom_{A_T}(A_T(1),A_T)$ for every $T$ over $S$. On the two standard charts with $t=x_1/x_0$, define $\mathcal O_P(1)$ by generators $e_0=t^{-1}e_1$. Let $c:A_P\to A_P(1)[2]$ be the Kummer first Chern class of $\mathcal O_P(1)$, obtained from the Kummer connecting homomorphism and derived scalar extension from $\mathbf Z/N$ to $A$. Put $K=A_S(-1)[-2]$. Define $h:K\to Rq_*A_P$ as the adjoint under $q^{-1}\dashv Rq_*$ of the composite $q^{-1}K\cong q^{-1}K\otimes_A^L A_P\xrightarrow{1\otimes c}q^{-1}K\otimes_A^L A_P(1)[2]\xrightarrow{\mathrm{ev}}A_P$, using twist pullback and evaluation. Write $1:A_S\to Rq_*A_P$ for the adjunction unit. Then

$$
(1,h):A_S\oplus A_S(-1)[-2]\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_*A_P
$$

is an isomorphism. For every morphism $g:S'\to S$, the corresponding projective-line square and ordinary-etale proper exchange identify the pullback of this isomorphism with the same construction over $S'$.

proof.text: The projection $q$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], hence finite type and quasi-compact. By [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft], $P$ is locally Noetherian. Its quasi-compactness follows because $q$ and $S$ are quasi-compact; thus $P$ is Noetherian. This checks the scheme hypotheses of the proper projection formula used next.

source.place: Proof final sentence: applicability of proper tensor projection

proof.text: By [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] there is an isomorphism $b_q:A_S(1)[2]\oplus A_S\to Rq_*A_P(1)[2]$ with the shifted twisted unit and Kummer adjoint as components. Tensor it by $K=A_S(-1)[-2]$ and apply [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] with $E=A_P(1)[2]$. The twists are locally free of rank one and pull back compatibly with tensor and evaluation by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]; evaluation identifies $q^{-1}K\otimes_A^L E$ with $A_P$. On a local rank-one basis evaluation is multiplication $A\otimes_A A\to A$, an isomorphism. The two source summands become $A_S$ and $K$. We have therefore obtained an isomorphism $A_S\oplus K\to Rq_*A_P$. No flatness of $A$ over $\mathbf Z/N$ is used.

source.place: Proof: projective-line decomposition and proper tensor projection

proof.text: Identify this isomorphism's components using [lem-amb-tensor-projection-adjunct]. Put $L=A_S(1)[2]$, $E=A_P(1)[2]$ and let $c:A_P\to E$ be the stated Chern class. Apply the lemma first to $a=\eta_{q,L}:L\to Rq_*E$, whose adjoint is the identity under twist pullback, and then to $a=Rq_*c\circ\eta_{q,A_S}:A_S\to Rq_*E$, whose adjoint is $c$. After the evaluation identifications of the preceding step, whose compatibility with inverse image, tensor and evaluation is [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], the first adjoint is $1_{A_P}$ and the second is $1_{q^{-1}K}\otimes c$ followed by evaluation. These define respectively $1$ and $h$. Thus the isomorphism just constructed is exactly $(1,h)$.

source.place: Proof: identification of the unit and Cartier-class components after tensor projection

proof.text: Let $g:S'\to S$ be arbitrary, $P'=P\times_SS'$, and write $g':P'\to P$, $q':P'\to S'$. The properness of $q$ is already checked and $A$ is a torsion ring since $N1_A=0$. Thus [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring] gives an isomorphism $\mathrm{Ex}:g^{-1}Rq_*A_P\to Rq'_*A_{P'}$. By [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] the source summands pull back to $A_{S'}\oplus A_{S'}(-1)[-2]$, with tensor/evaluation compatibility. Invertibility of $N$ pulls back. No Noetherian hypothesis on $S'$ is required.

source.place: Proof: arbitrary change of base, using torsion-ring proper exchange

proof.text: Let $D=(x_0=0)\subset P$. On the chart $x_1\ne0$ its ideal is $(s)$ in $B[s]$, with $s=x_0/x_1$; on $x_0\ne0$ its ideal is the unit ideal. Multiplication by $s$ is injective over every ring $B$ by comparison of polynomial coefficients, also after arbitrary base change. Thus $D$ and its pullback $D'\subset P'$ are effective Cartier divisors. The dual ideal generators are $e_0=1$ and $e_1=s^{-1}$, hence $e_0=s e_1=t^{-1}e_1$. They give $\mathcal O(D)=\mathcal O_P(1)$ and $\mathcal O(D')=\mathcal O_{P'}(1)$ with exactly the statement's convention.

source.place: Proof: the Cartier class of infinity under arbitrary base change

proof.text: Write $i:D\hookrightarrow P$, $i':D'\hookrightarrow P'$ and $u_D:A_P\to Ri_*A_D$. The supported Kummer lemma [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] gives $c_1(\mathcal O_P(1))=c_{D,A}u_D$ and $g'^{-1}c_{D,A}=c_{D',A}\mathrm{Ex}_i$, using the divisor check in the preceding step. The exchange of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] is a mate. The mate unit identity [lem-pur-mate-unit-compatibility], applied to this closed-immersion square with $\alpha$ the inverse-image square isomorphism, says $\mathrm{Ex}_i\circ g'^{-1}u_D=u_{D'}$ under the constant-sheaf identifications. Composing these two equations proves $g'^{-1}c=c'$, the Kummer class of $\mathcal O_{P'}(1)$.

source.place: Proof: pullback compatibility of the Cartier/Kummer component

proof.text: For the projective-line square apply the mate unit identity [lem-pur-mate-unit-compatibility] and the mate counit identity [lem-amb-mate-unit-counit] to the exchange defined in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. The unit identity gives $\mathrm{Ex}\circ g^{-1}(1)=1'$. For the other component the counit identity, precomposed with $q'^{-1}g^{-1}h$, gives the adjunct of $\mathrm{Ex}\circ g^{-1}h$ as the pullback of the adjunct of $h$; naturality of the inverse-image square comparison makes its source $q'^{-1}g^{-1}K$. By [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], the bifunctoriality of the inverse-image tensor comparison [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] (which moves $g'^{-1}(1\otimes c)$ to $1\otimes g'^{-1}c$), and $g'^{-1}c=c'$ from the preceding step, this is $1\otimes c'$ followed by evaluation. It is exactly the adjunct defining $h'$. Therefore $\mathrm{Ex}\circ g^{-1}(1,h)=(1,h')$. Its left side is a composite of isomorphisms, proving the required arbitrary-base compatibility and the isomorphism over $S'$.

source.place: Proof sentence: both defining components commute with arbitrary base change

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $q:P=\mathbf P^1_S\to S$, with $S$ Noetherian.
Let $h$ be the Kummer first Chern class of $\mathcal O_P(1)$.
Then

$$
(1,h):A_S\oplus A_S(-1)[-2]\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_*A_P
$$

is an isomorphism, compatible with arbitrary change of $S$.

proof.text:
For $\mathbf Z/n$-coefficients, the map is globally
defined by the unit and the Cartier class of infinity in
[lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map]. On a geometric fibre,
[thm-sc-proper-cohomology] gives cohomology only in
degrees $0,2$, each free of rank one; the genus is zero.
In its Kummer description, the degree-two map is
$\operatorname{Pic}(\mathbf P^1)/n\to H^2(\mathbf P^1,\mu_n)$,
and the class of $\mathcal O(1)$, of degree one, generates.
Thus $(1,h)$ is an isomorphism on every geometric fibre.
By [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite], [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]
it is an isomorphism on $S$. Both defining components
commute with base change, so the isomorphism does too. For
general $A$, tensor this isomorphism over $\mathbf Z/n$
with $A$ and use
[lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection].
